rating.verdict: Strong individual cards (Psychic Frog, Nethergoyf, Thoughtseize, Fatal Push) in a homebrew Sultai shell. Competitive at FNM, but slower and clunkier than the tuned Dimir midrange lists in the 2026 metagame.
strengths: Excellent cheap interaction: Thoughtseize, Fatal Push, Counterspell
Psychic Frog and the goyfs grow into big threats
weaknesses: Four-mana creatures (Chupacabra, Troll) are clunky in Modern
Three-color mana costs life from fetches and shocks
Can lose races to fast combo and aggro

wins: Sultai midrange: cheap cryptids that keep growing, backed by discard, removal and counterspells. Grind the opponent out, then finish with Troll or the Loch Ness serpent.
plan: Thoughtseize their best card, Fatal Push their first creature, and land a Goyf or Psychic Frog.
Fill the graveyard with different card types (fetchlands, Bauble, Consider) to grow Tarmogoyf and Nethergoyf. Exiling cards to Frog grows Cosmogoyf.
Flash in Lochmere Serpent at the end of their turn; Troll of Khazad-dûm needs three blockers.
keys: Discard to grow it, exile three graveyard cards for flying, draw when it connects.
Power equals the number of card types in the graveyard.
Destroys an opponent’s creature when it enters.
Counter or destroy, scaling with their graveyard.
tips: Card types: artifact, creature, enchantment, instant, sorcery, land, planeswalker, battle, kindred.
Discarding to Psychic Frog is a cost: do it at instant speed to save the Frog from damage.
Cycle Troll for 1 to fetch a Swamp when you need lands early.
mulligan: Keep 2–3 lands with a cheap threat and an interaction spell.
